artifact_comparison.determinism: Every repetition must have the same seven artifact hashes for its label and workload.
artifact_comparison.provenance_rule: Every packager hash and each present verifier hash must match the actual script. The candidate verifier hash is required; the baseline may predate it.
artifact_comparison.rule: Six files must match byte-for-byte. Parsed manifests must match after removing only packager_sha256 and source_verifier_sha256.

baseline.scope: Only the two packaging scripts come from this commit; all other inputs use the same current snapshot.

caveats: This is a packaging calibration on three small existing arithmetic workloads, with no timing-based pass threshold.
It does not establish an OCaml compilation-speed, Lean parity, Kan foundation, or Telcoin conformance claim.
Both script versions use one identical current compiler/input snapshot; this does not compare complete historical compiler versions.
Warm filesystem caches and installed dependencies are reused. Cold or incremental compiler builds are outside this measurement.
Host load, scheduling, power state, and thermal behavior can affect short process measurements. No CPU pinning or machine isolation is imposed.
Alternating paired runs reduces order bias but does not remove measurement noise; ratios are informational.

measurement_scope.cache_state: Existing dependencies and filesystem caches reused; all private input snapshots copied before timing; every output directory is fresh.
measurement_scope.excluded: Compiler build, snapshot preparation and hashing, baseline extraction, artifact comparison, and report serialization.
measurement_scope.included: Python startup, full source-lock verification, compiler startup/checking/emission, and all seven artifact writes into a fresh output directory.

settings.order: Alternate baseline/candidate order each round; rotate workload order each round.
settings.parallelism: One packaged compilation at a time.
settings.percentile_method: Nearest rank: sorted samples at ceil(n * 0.95) - 1.
